question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we rewrite the integral as

$$
\int (5x-2)^{1/2}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Now, we let $u=5x-2.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=5\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{5}\text{d}u.
$$

We now write our integral in terms of $u,$ calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (5x-2)^{1/2}\,\text{d}x & =\int {u}^{1/2}\cdot (\frac{1}{5})\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\int {u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot \frac{2}{3}{u}^{3/2}+C \\  & =\frac{2}{15}{u}^{3/2}+C \\  & =\frac{2}{15}(5x-2)^{3/2}+C \\  & =\frac{2}{15}\sqrt{(5x-2)^{3}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's double-check that our result is correct. If we differentiate the result, then it should come out to the original integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\frac{2}{15}\sqrt{(5x-2)^{3}}+C] & =\frac{2}{15}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\sqrt{(5x-2)^{3}}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =\frac{2}{15}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[(5x-2)^{3/2}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =\frac{2}{15}\cdot \frac{3}{2}(5x-2)^{1/2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5x-2)+0 \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(5x-2)^{1/2}\cdot 5 \\  & =(5x-2)^{1/2} \\  & =\sqrt{5x-2}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}z}[-\frac{2}{9}\sqrt{-32-9z}+C] & =-\frac{2}{9}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}z}[\sqrt{-32-9z}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}z}(C) \\  & =-\frac{2}{9}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}z}[(-32-9z)^{1/2}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}z}(C) \\  & =-\frac{2}{9}\cdot \frac{1}{2}(-32-9z)^{-1/2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}z}(-32-9z)+0 \\  & =-\frac{1}{9}\cdot (-32-9z)^{-1/2}\cdot (-9) \\  & =(-32-9z)^{-1/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{-32-9z}}\,✓\end{aligned}

\int (x+79)^{7/4}\,\text{d}x.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (x+79)^{7/4}\,\text{d}x & =\int {u}^{7/4}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{{u}^{11/4}}{11/4}+C \\  & =\frac{4}{11}(x+79)^{11/4}+C \\  & =\frac{4}{11}\sqrt[4]{(x+79)^{11}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's double-check that our result is correct. If we differentiate the result, then it should come out to the original integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\frac{4}{11}\sqrt[4]{(x+79)^{11}}+C] & =\frac{4}{11}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\sqrt[4]{(x+79)^{11}}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =\frac{4}{11}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[(x+79)^{11/4}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =\frac{4}{11}\cdot \frac{11}{4}(x+79)^{7/4}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x+79)+0 \\  & =(x+79)^{7/4}\cdot 1 \\  & =\sqrt[4]{(x+79)^{7}}\,✓\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}[-\frac{3}{5}\sqrt[3]{-88-5s}+C] & =-\frac{3}{5}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}[\sqrt[3]{-88-5s}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(C) \\  & =-\frac{3}{5}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}[(-88-5s)^{1/3}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(C) \\  & =-\frac{3}{5}\cdot \frac{1}{3}(-88-5s)^{-2/3}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-88-5s)+0 \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}(-88-5s)^{-2/3}\cdot (-5) \\  & =(-88-5s)^{-2/3} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{(-88-5s)^{2}}}\,✓\end{aligned}
